method: Inspect all six fixed desktop/mobile screenshots against preserved old-standard pages. Count substantive task-related structure/typography, not renamed concepts, extra content or recoloring. No rerolls.

topics.name: academic
topics.observation: Serif long-form narrative and separate contact column are coherent, but the original already had a three-part research sequence. Larger identity typography and a later mobile directory do not establish a substantial overall improvement.

topics.name: copy
topics.observation: Independent note grid, category presentation and individual copy controls support scanning and taking a single snippet. Mobile remains usable. Keyword filtering and copy were replayed; the multi-option sort does not match its declared single-field contract and remains a recorded limitation.

topics.name: calendar
topics.observation: A month grid with compact current-date header and adjacent upcoming events creates a materially different date-navigation structure. Mobile keeps the calendar within the viewport. Content problem: the highlighted 8th disagrees with the 7th in the current-date header, so structural improvement does not establish complete correctness.

topics.name: comparison
topics.observation: Large introductory block, summary metrics and product cards delay comparison. The old scenario controls and direct comparison table already supported this task. More cards do not establish improvement.

topics.name: docs
topics.observation: Risk reference sidebar and chapter links are useful, but the original already provided chapter navigation and a reference table. On mobile the risk reference precedes the main content. No clear overall structural improvement.

topics.name: essay
topics.observation: Spacious serif introduction and a featured excerpt retain the old single-column journal composition. The added whitespace and changed text do not establish a new reading organization.

reviewObservation: Copy review includes useful sort-contract evidence but also aesthetic note-height alignment and optional wording changes. Calendar review assumes a Search needs in-page results and speculates Append has no content source. Do not convert these comments into per-example prompt restrictions. Final copy/calendar selections retain Original.
decision: Keep opt-in disabled by default. Six final successes and five first-pass successes show compatibility, not sufficient visual breadth. Retain the observed defects without demanding perfection or claiming all interactions were verified. No new paid same-site sample while this gate is unmet.
